knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Vectorized reduction width boundary causes incorrect output for high-precision GPU reductions
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend-specific vectorized kernels may have hidden width or alignment boundaries, and high-precision dtypes can expose incorrect partial vectorization or boundary indexing during reductions.

risk_dimensions.shape: Reduction dimension widths near CUDA vectorization boundaries, especially with row count greater than one
risk_dimensions.dtype: High-precision floating dtypes such as torch.float64
risk_dimensions.memory: Contiguous and non-contiguous layouts may interact with vectorized kernel selection
risk_dimensions.device: CUDA and other GPU backends with specialized reduction kernels
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Reduction along a non-leading dimension with multiple rows

failure_mechanism.description: A vectorized high-precision reduction kernel on GPU mis-handles boundary widths, causing incorrect output or violation of reduction invariants such as row sums.

input_exploration: Sweep reduction dimension widths around vectorization boundaries and vary row counts
Test high-precision dtypes such as float64 on GPU backends
Explore shapes that may trigger partial vectorization in reduction kernels
Include contiguous and non-contiguous tensor layouts
constraint_awareness: Reduction dimension choice can select different kernel implementations
High-precision dtype behavior may differ between CPU and GPU
Backend kernel selection may depend on shape and dtype combinations
oracle_strategy: Compare GPU output against a CPU high-precision reference
Check that each output row sums to one within a small tolerance
Compare high-precision GPU output with lower-precision GPU output to isolate dtype-specific kernel issues

transferability.reason: The underlying principle applies to other GPU reduction-like operations that use vectorized kernels and high-precision dtypes, such as log_softmax, normalized reductions, or attention score normalization, but the specific boundary conditions may vary by kernel implementation.

important_considerations: Target reduction-like GPU kernels with high-precision floating dtypes
Vary reduction dimension widths across vectorization boundaries
Combine shape and dtype conditions that may select specialized backend kernels
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that sweep reduction widths, dtypes, and memory layouts on GPU, compare results against CPU reference implementations, and verify mathematical invariants rather than hard-coding a specific triggering shape.
